title: Some of the first colour movies were painted by hand, straight onto the film

cover.alt: A hand-tinted frame from an 1890s film: a dancer on a small stage raises a huge pink skirt like wings against a dark backdrop.
cover.credit: Edison Manufacturing Co. (W. K. L. Dickson, William Heise) · Public domain

body: Early films were shot in black and white, so any colour had to be added afterwards. Edison’s *Annabelle Serpentine Dance* films, among the earliest examples, were coloured by painting **aniline dyes** straight onto the emulsion. In Paris, Elisabeth Thuillier later ran a studio of **220 women** who hand-coloured films for Georges Méliès, painting directly on the film stock with brushes. Each worker was given one colour, assembly-line style, and a single film often used more than 20.

slides.alt: A hand-tinted 1890s film of a dancer on a small stage swirling a huge skirt; its colour jumps between yellow, white and pink from moment to moment.
slides.caption: A dancer swirls a vast skirt in Annabelle Serpentine Dance, an 1895 Edison film. The print was tinted by hand, so its colours flicker from yellow to white to pink.
slides.credit: Edison Manufacturing Co. (W. K. L. Dickson, William Heise) · Public domain · excerpt
slides.music: “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairies” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.question: Elisabeth Thuillier’s Paris studio coloured films by hand. How many women painted there?
slides.explanation: About 220 women, painting directly on the film stock with brushes in the colours Thuillier chose. Her lab coloured films for Georges Méliès.

slides.heading: Of about 60 hand-coloured copies of A Trip to the Moon, one is known to survive
slides.note: Coloured by the Thuillier lab for Georges Méliès’s 1902 film

slides.question: How did Thuillier’s studio share out the work of colouring a film?
options: Each painter took one whole reel
A machine sprayed on the dyes
Whole scenes were dipped in dye
slides.explanation: Assembly-line style: each worker was assigned a different colour, and more than 20 separate colours were often used on a single film.
